evidence: src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService's constructor injects OrderRepository and ProductRepository, and every persistence call goes through these abstractions (findById, save, list, listByState).
src/application/order-service.ts: state changes go through domain methods: order.advanceTo(state), order.cancel(), products[index].reserve(line.quantity), product.release(line.quantity).
src/application/order-service.ts: lookup-or-throw is defined once each in requiredProduct and requiredOrder, and view mapping once each in toProductView and toOrderView.

src/application/order-service.ts: ensureStockIsAvailable(lines, products) adds up the requested quantity per product and checks it before any reservation (a check across several aggregates), but it ignores its products parameter ('void products;') and fetches each product again with requiredProduct, which is redundant but not a bypass.

src/application/order-service.ts: the class comment 'Coordinates the fulfilment use cases using domain repository abstractions' matches its public methods addProduct, placeOrder, changeState, cancelOrder, listOrders and listProducts.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is one file, src/application/order-service.ts, with one class, OrderService, and three DTO interfaces (PlaceOrderInput, ProductView, OrderView). All of it serves one concern: the fulfilment use cases. The service creates products, places orders while reserving stock, moves orders between states, cancels orders while releasing stock, and lists orders and products.

It uses its abstractions consistently:
- It reaches persistence only through the injected OrderRepository and ProductRepository.
- It changes state only through domain methods: Order.advanceTo, Order.cancel, Product.reserve and Product.release.
- It reports failures with DomainError.
- Lookup-or-throw lives in one place each (requiredProduct, requiredOrder), and so does view mapping (toProductView, toOrderView).

The stock check in ensureStockIsAvailable adds up the quantities for each product across all lines and checks every product before any reservation. That check spans several aggregates, so it reasonably belongs in the application layer. Without the Product source, I can't show that it repeats a single-product invariant inside Product.reserve.

One smell: ensureStockIsAvailable takes a products parameter, ignores it with `void products`, and fetches each product again through requiredProduct. This is redundant work but not a bypass, since it still goes through the module's own helper and repository. It is too weak to count as a rubric failure.
